4th Period.workingNow: Naming the feeling you want your mod to create, and finishing all three letters of your MDA design.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One design document in your portfolio repo bringing together your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic and state map — plus your ROLLER game embedded and playable on your portfolio site — pushed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can name the dynamics and aesthetic of my mod so that my mechanics have a reason to exist.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: I do: D and A — what players actually feel (12 min)
We do: name the base game's aesthetic (8 min)
You do: finish your full MDA design (22 min)
Exit Ticket: your one-word aesthetic (3 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you listed mechanics — the rules. Today you name what those rules make players feel, and why anyone would want to play your version. Tomorrow you take the single mechanic you care most about and work out the states it needs.

6th Period.workingNow: Drawing the arrows between your two states and labeling what makes each one happen.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your completed Game Plan document — two mechanics each with a number, five states, how the mechanics connect to the states, and your first level described — typed and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can name the trigger that switches between my two states so that my diagram shows how the thing actually changes.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including nested loops and compound conditionals.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Quick overview: today we add arrows (2 min)
I do: what a trigger is — the door (10 min)
We do: add triggers to yesterday's lamp (10 min)
You do: draw your 2 states + their triggers (22 min)
Exit Ticket: one trigger, in a full sentence (3 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday you named two states. Today you answer the only question left: what makes it switch? That is a trigger, and it is the arrow between two boxes. Tomorrow we add a third state and things get more interesting.
